outcomes.description: Transform the image into a pencil drawing.

nodes.question: Compared with the supplied source image, how fully has the edited image been transformed into a pencil drawing?
nodes.criteria: complete: across the image as a whole, pencil-drawing rendering is pervasive, with visible drawn pencil marks, texture, and shading replacing the source's photographic appearance; color may remain if the overall rendering is convincingly pencil-drawn. partial: some pencil-like marks, texture, shading, or related transformation is evident, but the image as a whole still substantially retains photographic rendering or is not consistently pencil-drawn. Desaturation or grayscale alone is not sufficient for complete. absent: no requested pencil-drawing transformation is evident. unknown: evidence is insufficient to determine progress. Unrelated edits do not count.
nodes.binding: Compare the supplied source image with the edited image. Assess whether the edited image has been transformed into a pencil drawing.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
